title: Hybrid Router and Token Smoother for Latency-stable Cost Tuning
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We want to safely apply batching and KV-prefetch/cache recommendations that reduce per-token cost without violating customer latency/throughput SLOs. Current automated recommendations sometimes cause tail latency spikes under mixed traffic because aggressive batching or cache reuse increases queueing and creates bursty backpressure.

Goal: Implement a hybrid routing layer plus a token-smoothing limiter that: 1) routes requests across model variants and capacity tiers with explicit SLO-awareness, 2) applies conservative per-cohort batching/caching patches in staged cohorts, and 3) automatically detects anomalies and performs automated rollback when SLO regressions are confirmed. The feature must integrate with the existing batching/caching recommender and Console rollout UI and emit telemetry for audit and postmortem analysis.
acceptance_criteria: A/B cohort canary flow that applies new batching/caching profile to 5% then 25% then 100% with automated hold or rollback triggers
SLO-aware router respects 95th and 99th latency budgets and avoids routing to variants when projected breach probability > 5%
Token-smoother limiter enforces per-second token send rate per instance to prevent queue buildup; integrated with autoscaler so capacity scaling is not masked

Anomaly detector raises automated rollback if latency or error-rate breaches persist for more than 3 minutes and are corroborated by independent signals (trace p95 upward trend + queue depth increase)
End-to-end integration tests and staged canary run show no customer-facing SLO violations on existing production traffic during patch application
Telemetry is emitted to Console: per-cohort latency distribution, rollback reason, and cost delta estimates
tasks: Design hybrid routing decision model (SLO-aware scoring function)
Implement token-smoother limiter with configurable windows and burst allowance
Hook recommender to new rollout API to create staged cohort configs
Build anomaly detector: multi-signal drift detector (latency p95/p99, queue depth, error rate)
Implement automated rollback orchestration and audit trail entry
Add Console UI bits: cohort rollout view, rollback justification, preview cost estimates
Create canary plan and run internal staging tests against replayed traffic
Add integration and chaos tests (simulate worker slowdown, network jitter, and cache miss storms)
Document runbook for manual override and follow-up forensic queries
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flags gated by customer tier. 2) Stage internally against production-like replay for 48h. 3) Canary 5% (30m), monitor metrics and anomaly signals. If green, expand to 25% (2h). If green, expand to 100% in waves with 15m watch windows. Automated rollback criteria active at each stage. Manual abort path available in Console.
metrics: tokens/sec served and tokens queued per instance
error rate (5xx and model failures) by cohort
cost delta per 1M tokens (estimated and realized)
canary progression time and hold reasons
risks: False-positive anomaly triggers could prevent beneficial cost reductions — mitigated by multi-signal confirmation and conservative thresholds
Overly conservative router may avoid cost-saving variants even when safe — mitigation: post-deploy A/B analysis and tunable risk budget per customer tier
Interaction with autoscaler: token-smoothing could hide load signals causing underprovisioning — mitigation: expose smoothing-adjusted metrics to autoscaler and keep smoothing budget bounded
Telemetry volume increase — mitigation: sampling and aggregated rollup for long-term retention
comments: 2026-02-12 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after postmortem of cost-savings incident where p99 spiked after aggressive prefetch profile was applied.
2026-02-18 Arjun Patel: Draft scoring function uploaded to the design doc; leaning toward a probabilistic budget that uses p95/p99 and queue slope to estimate breach risk.
2026-02-25 Design review: Recommend token-smoother use a leaky-bucket with short and long windows (200ms, 10s) and a small burst allowance tied to instance capacity.
2026-03-03 Engineering sync: Decided anomaly detector will require two corroborating signals (latency trend + queue depth) OR latency spike + increased 5xx for automated rollback.
2026-03-10 QA: Integration tests for staged rollout passing in staging replay; flagged a race between autoscaler metrics and smoothed signals — added task to expose smoothing-adjusted metrics.
2026-03-14 Arjun Patel: Implemented initial router and limiter prototype; running internal replay for 24h. Next: add integration with recommender and Console hooks.
